title: The central semisimple tangent subspace is a restricted invariant subalgebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], with an algebraic closure $\bar k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All group schemes are affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroup schemes are closed [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smooth and connected mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Tori and groups of multiplicative type have the meanings of [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type]. For a smooth group $J$, write $\mathfrak j=T_{J/k,e}$ [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], with bracket induced by commutators [def-wf-lie-algebra]; $\operatorname{Ad}$ is the differential of conjugation. Fix a faithful closed linear representation of $J$ into $\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group]. A tangent vector is semisimple if its matrix in this representation is diagonalizable over $\bar k$, and is central if its bracket with every tangent vector is zero. Nilpotent for a group means that it has a finite descending central series of closed normal subgroup schemes with commutators lowering the series. In characteristic $p>0$, $X^{[p]}$ denotes the tangent vector whose left invariant derivation on $k[J]$ is the $p$-fold composite of the derivation of $X$. A restricted Lie subalgebra means a $k$-linear subspace closed under brackets and $X\mapsto X^{[p]}$. Let $J$ be smooth and connected, assume that $J$ is not nilpotent, and suppose every semisimple element of $\mathfrak j_{\bar k}$ is central. Then $k$ has positive characteristic $p$. The set $\mathfrak s(J)=\{X\in\mathfrak j:X\text{ is semisimple}\}$ is a restricted Lie subalgebra, and the adjoint action of $J$ on this subspace is trivial as a group-scheme representation. Moreover $\bar k\otimes_k\mathfrak s(J)$ is exactly the subspace of all semisimple elements of $\mathfrak j_{\bar k}$.

source.place: Proposition 17.80 proof, printed p.378, first reduction paragraph; Corollary 17.77, p.377 (central semisimple vectors are fixed by the group). The scalar-extension formulation makes explicit the geometric subspace needed in that reduction.

proof.text: Suppose $\operatorname{char}k=0$. For $Y\in\mathfrak j$, apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-lie-additive-jordan] over the perfect field $k$ to write $Y=Y_s+Y_n$. The semisimple vector $Y_s$ is central by the geometric hypothesis, hence $\operatorname{ad}(Y)=\operatorname{ad}(Y_n)$. The same node, for the rational adjoint representation, says this last endomorphism is nilpotent. Thus every adjoint operator is nilpotent. [lem-sfb-charzero-ad-nilpotence-group-criterion] makes $J$ nilpotent, contrary to hypothesis. Consequently $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ for a prime $p$.

Identify $\mathfrak j$ with its image in $\operatorname{Mat}_n(k)$ under the fixed faithful differential, injective by [lem-sfb-algebraic-lie-additive-jordan]. Let $Z=\{X\in\mathfrak j:[X,Y]=0\text{ for every }Y\in\mathfrak j\}$. These are homogeneous linear equations, so $Z$ is a vector subspace; solving these equations by row reduction also gives $Z_{\bar k}=Z(\mathfrak j_{\bar k})$. Matrices in $Z$ commute. By [lem-sfb-restricted-rational-differentiation], matrix $p$th power represents the restricted operation and $\operatorname{ad}(X^{[p]})=\operatorname{ad}(X)^p$. Hence $Z$ is closed under $p$th powers.

Apply [lem-sfb-commuting-p-power-stable-image] to the commuting matrix space $Z$. Its stable image $Z_\infty$ is a $k$-linear subspace closed under $p$th powers, consisting exactly of the geometrically diagonalizable matrices in $Z$. Every semisimple vector of $\mathfrak j$ lies in $Z$ by hypothesis, and conversely a diagonalizable member of $Z$ is semisimple by the stated definition. Thus $\mathfrak s(J)=Z_\infty$. The same argument over $\bar k$, using $Z_{\bar k}=Z(\mathfrak j_{\bar k})$ and the geometric centrality hypothesis, identifies $\bar k\otimes_k\mathfrak s(J)$ with all geometric semisimple elements. Since $[Z,Z]=0$ and $0$ is semisimple, brackets of elements of $\mathfrak s(J)$ belong to it. Matrix $p$th powers are restricted powers by step 2, giving the restricted Lie subalgebra assertion.

source.place: 17.80 first reduction, p.378; explicit stable-image descent.

proof.text: For each $X\in\mathfrak s(J)$, [lem-sfb-semisimple-tangent-stabilizer] gives a smooth closed adjoint stabilizer $C\subseteq J$ with $\operatorname{Lie}(C)=\mathfrak j$, since $X$ is central. Work over $F=\bar k$. Connectedness of $J_F$ follows from [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected], applied to the identity section. The base change $C_F$ is smooth over $F$. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-group-identity-subgroup], $(C_F)^0$ is a connected open and closed subgroup. It is smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]. Its tangent space equals that of $C_F$: a dual-number point at the identity factors through this open subscheme, since its underlying space has only that point. By the scalar-extension isomorphism of [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus], natural in the inclusion $C\to J$, the image of $\operatorname{Lie}(C_F)\cong F\otimes_k\operatorname{Lie}(C)=F\otimes_k\mathfrak j$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(J_F)\cong F\otimes_k\mathfrak j$ is everything. So the tangent space of $(C_F)^0$ spans $\operatorname{Lie}(J_F)$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-subgroup-tangent-generation] with the one subgroup $(C_F)^0$ and containing subgroup $C_F$ to get $C_F=J_F$. Writing $C$ as the quotient by an ideal $I$ of $k[J]$, this equality says $I\otimes_k F=0$, so $I=0$: any nonzero vector in $I$ would remain nonzero after extension of a vector-space basis. Thus $C=J$ as group schemes.

Choose a $k$-basis $X_1,\ldots,X_r$ of $\mathfrak s(J)$. Step 4 says that for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and $g\in J(A)$ one has $\operatorname{Ad}(g)(X_i\otimes1)=X_i\otimes1$ for each $i$. By $A$-linearity, $\operatorname{Ad}(g)(\sum_i a_i(X_i\otimes1))=\sum_i a_i(X_i\otimes1)$ for every tuple $(a_i)\in A^r$. This is precisely triviality of the group-scheme representation on $\mathfrak s(J)$, including $r=0$.

The item restates the 17.80 sentence: if G is not nilpotent and every geometric semisimple element is central, then char p>0 and the semisimple vectors form an Ad-stable p-Lie subalgebra. It adds the clause that kbar tensor s(J) is the whole geometric semisimple subspace. Step 1: the Jordan node, applied to the embedding and to Ad, gives ad(Y)=ad(Y_n) nilpotent; with the new char-0 criterion this is a contradiction. Step 2: by restricted-rational-differentiation, the centre Z is a commuting matrix space closed under p-th powers. Step 3: the stable-image lemma gives s(J)=Z_inf and its kbar base change. Step 4: the smooth stabilizer C has full Lie algebra, and tangent-generation over kbar gives C=J. Step 5 (elementary) is correct. The new nodes are all true and none duplicates an existing node. (a) Char-0 criterion: Engel, then Ad G unipotent and ker Ad=Z(G) in char 0, so G is nilpotent; it fails in char p (G_a semidirect G_m with weight p). (b) Stable image: I checked every clause, including the base-change formula from a basis, the semilinear bijection on the semisimple subspace S over kbar, and W cap (kbar tensor W_inf)=W_inf. (c) Stabilizer node = Milne 17.76. I searched both Lie chapters; adjoint-kernel-central-quotient, lie-normalizer-centralizer, infinite-field-centralizer-reduction, semisimple-derivation-zero-smooth and lem-ag-lie-centre are not duplicates.
